title: lab.common.memory wired into brain.reason as memory_path=, a persistent cross-call note cache that refuses to trust a stale or missing source
goal: Give lab.common.memory -- a confirmed-dormant module matching the project owner's 'brain RAM, not bounded by context length' architecture question -- its first real wiring into brain.reason, without faking the 'archive' revalidation depends on (the reason a shallow wiring was deliberately deferred earlier in this same session).
method: One fact, written once via a real lookup_fallback answer, then recalled under three conditions: its source passage still present and byte-identical (must revalidate); its source passage absent from the call entirely (must report missing_source, not reuse the note); its source passage present but with DIFFERENT text at the same id (must report version_mismatch AND still answer correctly from the new text). A fifth call with memory_path omitted checks zero behavior change for every existing caller.
results_prose: Write: decision='supported', text='30 days [P1]'. Recall with the same passage still present and unchanged: [{'note_id': 'e69836956f8656b2f7b1c623', 'valid': True, 'statement': 'The notice period is 30 days.', 'chunk_id': 'P1'}] (valid=True). Recall with the passage absent this call: [{'note_id': 'e69836956f8656b2f7b1c623', 'valid': False, 'reason': 'missing_source'}] (correctly missing_source=True). Recall with the passage PRESENT but its text CHANGED: [{'note_id': 'e69836956f8656b2f7b1c623', 'valid': False, 'reason': 'version_mismatch'}] (correctly version_mismatch=True) -- and the system still answers correctly from the new text ('60 days now, updated policy [P1]'), never from the stale cached note. With memory_path omitted entirely: no memory_recall step at all, decision unaffected (True).
conclusion: lab.common.memory is now wired into lab.common.brain.reason as its persistent, cross-call memory (memory_path=, default None, zero regression for every existing caller), narrowly scoped to the one place a fact maps cleanly onto its schema (lookup_fallback's single verbatim span). The full cycle works end to end: a verified note is written, recalled correctly when its source is still present and unchanged, and -- the part that would have been wrong with a shallow wiring -- correctly refused when its source is absent or has changed, with the system falling back to fresh extraction rather than ever trusting a stale note blindly.
scale_down: One fact, one passage id, three revalidation conditions -- a proof the write/recall/revalidate cycle is wired correctly and refuses to trust stale/missing sources, not a capacity or performance benchmark for the note store at scale.
follow_ups: Only wired at lookup_fallback's single-span-single-passage answer shape -- document_write, forward_chain, and rule-gate answers are not written as notes at all (their answer shape doesn't map onto memory.py's schema as directly); a dedicated design pass would be needed to decide what, if anything, those paths should write.

memory.mark_conflicted is not wired -- nothing today compares a freshly-extracted answer against a still-valid recalled note and flags disagreement; this would parallel lab.common.working_memory's cross-page contradiction check but for cross-call facts instead.

memory_recall is reported in trace only, never used to answer directly or skip extraction -- the same 'report, don't act on it yet' posture coherence_flags/contract_violations started with; a future pass could decide whether a valid, high-confidence recall should ever short-circuit re-extraction.
models_used: None -- memory.py's write/recall/revalidate is pure deterministic SQLite + string/hash comparison; the lookup_fallback answer it wraps uses whichever extractor the caller already selected (use_real_qa or the classical default), unchanged by this wiring.
